formula: conc ~ SSfpl(age, A, B, xmid, scal) + (A + B + xmid + scal|Lot)
notes: NONLINEAR: Read the help page (Davidian and Giltinan 1995; Pinheiro and Bates 2000 App A.11); the page has no model. P&B 2000 section 4.2 fits Lot as random in a linear model, lme(conc ~ age, IGF, random = pdDiag(~age)) (nlme's scripts/ch04.R), not the four-parameter logistic this formula recalls. RULE GAP: nonlinear mixed model; formula is pseudo-lme4.

Read PBG.Rd (App. A.21; Venables and Ripley 2002 s. 10.3). Page gives no model; rendered from the design (five rabbits, each under Placebo and MDL 72222, increasing doses) and the V&R analysis. Run identifies the rabbit-by-treatment combination and is ignored. V&R 2002 section 10.3 fits Rabbit as random on MASS's copy of these data (Rabbit, the rabbit as Animal), a four-parameter logistic in log dose with random A + ld50 ~ 1 | Animal and then Animal/Run (MASS scripts/ch10.R); this formula simplifies it to a linear trend in log(dose). RULE GAP: log transform of dose.

Read Relaxin.Rd (no model, no details). Filed as the groupedData default cAMP ~ conc | Run. RULE GAP: the book analyses this dose-response assay with a nonlinear (logistic-type) curve, not a linear one. Hand sample #12: the groupedData descriptor does not establish a fitted linear mixed model. The S-PLUS nlme help page for these data (Bioassay of the Protein Relaxin, Examples) fits Run as random, nlme(nlsList(cAMP ~ fpl(conc, A, B, ld50, scal), data = Relaxin, cluster = ~ Run)); this formula simplifies that four-parameter logistic to a linear trend in conc.

formula: Goals ~ Gender + Grade + Age + Race + Urban/Rural + (1|School)
notes: RESPONSE INFERRED: DASL PopularKids (Chase & Dummer 1992); students in 9 schools report most important goal (Goals: Grades/Sports/Popular), School the clustering unit. Grades/Sports/Looks/Money are the four-factor rankings (alternate outcomes), ignored. No model documented; formula is the natural random-intercept over School. Retained School assumes exchangeable sampling from a larger population of schools; this remains unverified.

RESPONSE INFERRED: figure-skating scores cross-classified by skating pair and judge; technical score (performance) the outcome, program the artistic score (alternate response, ignored), pcountry/jcountry the nationalities behind the nationalistic-bias question. Labels sparse. Hand pass #82: exercise 9.7 models the program score with a same-country indicator in place of additive nationality effects; the raw pcountry and jcountry stay the covariates. The inferred performance response is overturned. MLMUS 4e exercise 9.7, in chapter 9 on crossed random effects, is recalled as fitting pair and judge as crossed random intercepts; its text was not re-read in the five-level recheck.

RESPONSE INFERRED: wheat variety trial, 10 varieties each grown on 6 plots; yield the outcome modelled with a variety random intercept, moist a moisture covariate, plot the replicate index. #24 cluster rule: variety repeats within the table and indexes the grouping. No labels. VERDICT 2026-10-08: the six plots are the blocks each of the ten varieties is grown in; block random, variety fixed, as leafblotch in #23 (blind reading). Hand pass #82: exercise 4.4's final fit, used for prediction, has a variety intercept and no slope; the 2026-10-08 fixed-variety, random-block reading is overturned. Littell et al. (2006, p. 320), as JMP's Example Using Mixed Model fits these data, also groups random effects by variety, its ten varieties randomly selected from a population of hard red winter wheat varieties.

formula: win ~ dist_focal + dist_other + n_focal + n_other + (1 | focal) + (1 | other) + (1 | dyad)
notes: RESPONSE INFERRED/empty help: primate intergroup contest, win for focal; focal, other and dyad repeated clusters; male/female composition counts are subsets of n, ignored. Lecture example, no book model. VERDICT 2026-10-08: the dyad is a grouping factor beside the two actor factors (blind reading); the second direction of a directed dyad is a further row (multivariate rule). Hand sample #61: chapter 14 fits its dyadic model to the KosterLeckie gifts, so no book fit establishes this formula. Retained focal, other and dyad assume exchangeable sampling from a larger population of capuchin groups and their pairs; this remains unverified.

rethinking Dinosaurs: body mass over age for 6 dinosaur species; the Rd describes the data and supplies no model. species repeats within the table so it is the grouping factor per the #24 rule, rendered as a random intercept and age slope at low confidence. sp_id duplicates species. Hand sample #61: no book fit supports the correlated age slope; the formula is inferred. Retained species assumes exchangeable sampling from a larger population of dinosaur species; this remains unverified.

RESPONSE INFERRED: ROS HDI (Ch 2, red-state/blue-state); hdi.Rmd makes descriptive plots, fits no model. The file is a 50-state x 9-election panel (1968-2000); a reader would model Democratic vote share on state income. st_state repeats and is rendered as a grouping per the election-table rule (#24) at low. st_year is a design factor by the five-level rule: nine presidential elections, 1968 to 2000, named periods rather than a sample. st_inc10k duplicates st_income; vote counts and the repshare alternate ignored.

formula: leaves ~ crown.mm + diam.1 + diam.2 + (1 | Genus) + (1 | Genus:Species)
notes: RESPONSE INFERRED: Leaf count is a proposed response with Species nested within Genus. Year is constant at 2004 and is omitted. The book’s chapter 6 concerns biomass/Gamma models; this leaf-count model is not verified as a published fit. Retained Genus assumes exchangeable sampling from a larger population of dipterocarp genera; this remains unverified.

formula: nlme::lme(Age ~ fStain*fLocation, random=~1|fSpecies/fDolphinID, weights=nlme::varIdent(form=~1|fLocation), method="REML", data=transform(subset(Cetaceans, Sex != 0), fStain=factor(Stain), fLocation=factor(Location), fSpecies=factor(Species), fDolphinID=factor(DolphinID)))
notes: Chapter 20 final M3 fits Gaussian Age with Stain-by-Location fixed effects, nested Species/DolphinID intercepts and location-specific residual variances, excluding Sex=0. The full Sex-by-Stain-by-Location model is fitted earlier, but Sex and its interactions are removed from the final fit. modeldiagramR's cetaceans examples also fit random = ~ 1|fSpecies/fDolphinID to these data.

formula: Nauplii ~ Volume + Depth + Production_week + Month + (1 | Station)
notes: RESPONSE INFERRED: Nauplii is retained as a proposed count response, with repeated Station as the cluster; stations include A, C, E, F and G. Chapter 9 instead models Copepod, using log Volume as an offset, Production_week smooths by Depth and fixed Station. The filed Nauplii formula is not a documented chapter fit. Retained Station assumes exchangeable sampling from a larger population of sampling stations; this remains unverified.

formula: wt ~ wingcrd + flatwing + tarsus + head + culmen + nalospi + Sex + Age + (1 | observer)
notes: RULE GAP: sparrow morphometrics. observer (each observer measured many birds) rendered as the measurement cluster (1|observer) per the #24 repeating-cluster rule, at low. SexNew derived from Sex; Speciescode near-constant. Hand sample #61: the author's chapter 8 code shows the weight distribution and a normal density; it fits no OLS model of weight on size. Retained observer assumes exchangeable sampling from a larger population of observers; this remains unverified.

formula: BMS10mg ~ OriginAltitude + GardenAltitude + InitSize + Soil + (1 | Location) + (1 | Garden) + (1 | Garden:Bed)
notes: RESPONSE INFERRED: BMS10mg is retained as a continuous proposed response. Origin Location crosses Garden, with Bed nested within Garden. The exact shoot/stem interpretation of BMS10mg and this additive fixed part were not independently verified from chapter code; chapter 9 describes reproductive indices with nested and crossed random effects. Retained Garden assumes exchangeable sampling from a larger population of common-garden sites; this remains unverified.

RULE GAP: orange-crowned warbler reproductive success (fledglings, zero-inflated count) vs breeding density and precipitation, nests grouped by Year. Few years makes the random year weak. Xloc/Yloc coordinates; band/nest ids ignored. Hand sample #12: the proposed Year random-effect model is unverified at the source; published_model no stands. Brooks et al. (2019, Ecology 100:e02706, Application to warbler fecundity) fit these nests with a random effect of year in the zero-inflation model, as the original study did (Sofaer et al. 2014a); this formula simplifies that zero-inflated Poisson model, with the year effect in the count part.
